messages:
anna_ml: Pushed an eval run for candidate model `fast-embed-1.2` vs our baseline `open-embed-1.0` on the wiki similarity set (10k pairs). Included fp16 and int8 quantized variants. Job: eval/789.
ci-bot: eval/789 finished — artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-evals/eval-789/ (metrics.csv, clusters/*.png, sample_pairs.jsonl) :white_check_mark:
liam_research: quick TL;DR from metrics.csv — baseline(open-1.0 fp16) recall@1 0.719, recall@5 0.908, recall@10 0.945. fast-embed-1.2 fp16 recall@1 0.732 (+1.8%), recall@5 0.914 (+0.7%), recall@10 0.948 (+0.3%). fast-embed-1.2 int8 recall@1 0.718 (-1.9% rel vs fp16), recall@5 0.905 (-1.0%), recall@10 0.937 (-1.1%).
chris_infra: Interesting — fp16 gives a small lift, int8 loses some recall. How about distributional differences / embedding drift?
morgan_pm: Can you share clustering/segmentation numbers? We care about nearest-neighbor quality for feature flags. :eyes:
liam_research: Clustering (kmeans, k=50) silhouette: open-1.0 fp16 0.42, fast-1.2 fp16 0.47 (better cluster structure), fast-1.2 int8 0.36 (significant drop). UMAP plots in artifacts show more overlap in int8.
anna_ml: Code used to run the quant path (for reproducibility):
```
python eval_similarity.py \
  --model fast-embed-1.2 \
  --precision int8 \
  --dataset wiki_pairs_10k.jsonl \
  --save-dir gs://redwood-evals/eval-789/
```
liam_research: Computed per-sample embedding deltas: `np.linalg.norm(e_fp16 - e_int8)` median ~0.09, 95th ~0.36. For the top-failing pairs (where rank dropped >5) median delta ~0.24.
chris_infra: Could be quantization scheme — we used symmetric per-tensor int8 here. Did you try per-channel or asymmetric per-tensor?
anna_ml: Not yet. I ran our fast path that packs weights with symmetric int8 + fast dequant kernel to match serving perf.
morgan_pm: Operational question — how does this impact cost if we keep fp16 instead? Rough estimate?
liam_research: Perf delta: int8 inference median latency down ~28% and cost/req down ~24% in sim env. fp16 baseline is pricier but higher quality for clustering.
anna_ml: Suggested next steps:
- Try per-channel quant + bias correction (likely to recover recall/cluster).
- Run a focused eval on the retrieval slice (hard negatives) and compute recall@k by difficulty bins.
- If per-channel still bad, test mixed precision: keys/queries fp16, rest int8.
- Add a small calibration set (1k examples) for quant tuning.

liam_research: Also proposing an AB rollout plan if we keep fp16 model: route 5% traffic to fast-embed-1.2 fp16 in staging/dedicated for 48h and monitor recall/regressions on our production eval hooks.
chris_infra: I'll provision a small dedicated instance for the AB and add tracing hooks (token-level latency, batch sizes).
morgan_pm: Sounds good. Anna, can you run per-channel quant + 1k calibration and post new eval artifacts? If the cluster silhouette for int8 improves to >0.43, we can consider int8 for non-critical buckets. :thinking:
anna_ml: On it — kicking off a per-channel quant run now (job eval/792). ETA ~2h. Will post results here. :rocket:
